baseline.pad_handling: sum token embeddings only over non-PAD positions, divide by the true non-PAD length clamped to a minimum of 1 to avoid divide-by-zero; an all-PAD input has a zero summed embedding so it produces an exact finite zero pooled vector

experimental_1.pad_handling: convolution-window-aware: for each kernel size, a window is only eligible for max-over-time pooling if every position it covers is non-PAD; windows touching any PAD position are masked to -inf so PAD can never create an artificial n-gram feature. If a sample has zero eligible windows for a given kernel size (e.g. all-PAD, or fewer real tokens than the kernel size), that kernel's pooled feature is set to a finite zero vector instead of -inf

experimental_2.pad_handling: use true (non-PAD) sequence lengths to pack sequences before the GRU so PAD steps are never processed as real input, and to correctly extract the final forward and final backward hidden states at each sequence's true last non-PAD position. Samples with zero non-PAD length are never passed into pack_padded_sequence (which requires length >= 1) -- they are excluded from the GRU call entirely and assigned a finite zero hidden representation directly
experimental_2.dropout_placement: num_layers=1, so nn.GRU's constructor dropout argument is set to 0 (it would otherwise silently no-op between layers anyway). The configured dropout=0.3 is applied as its own explicit nn.Dropout layer on the final concatenated forward+backward hidden vector, before the linear classifier head
